title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a lecture sketch on computing the integral homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces as non-additive derived functors. The previous page covers the décalage (Quillen–Illusie/Bousfield) and the Koszul complexes linking Sym, Λ and Γ.

(1) Heading and claim: Dold–Puppe ('Homologie nicht-additiver Funktoren', Ann. Inst. Fourier 1961). For a module M (or a chain complex M_• of A-modules, 'at least for M concentrated in one degree'), take the Dold–Kan simplicial object and apply a functor F degreewise; the homotopy groups are L_iF(M_•). For F = the identity Z-module functor one gets L_i Z M_* = H_i(M_*). The key claim is L_r Sym^*_Z ≃ L_r Z[ ]: derived symmetric algebra equals derived group-ring functor.

(2) Since Sym = ⊕_j Sym^j, L_i Sym(M_*) carries an extra grading. This is 'la graduation par le poids' on the homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces.

(3) Key point, Dold–Thom: Sym^∞X = * ∪ X ∪ X^(2) ∪ … satisfies π_i Sym^∞X ≃ H̃_i X, because X ↦ π_* Sym^∞X satisfies the Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms. Equivalently π_i Z X = H_i X, where ZX is the free simplicial abelian group.

(4) Take X = M(G,n) a Moore space (e.g. G = Z^k × finite). Then Sym^∞ M(G,n) ~ K(G,n), and Z M(G,n) ~ K(G,n) as simplicial abelian groups, by definition / Dold–Kan.

(5) Dold's theorem: Z[Sym^∞X] ≅ Sym(Z X). Degreewise, the group ring of the free commutative monoid on a set is the polynomial ring on it. Hence
H_i(K(G,n)) = π_i Z[K(G,n)] = π_i Z[Sym^∞ M(G,n)] = π_i Sym(Z M(G,n)) = L_i Sym(G,n).
So the homology of K(G,n) is the derived functor of Sym on G[n], and it inherits the weight grading.

(6) Stability: H_{n+r} K(M,n) ≃ H_{n+r+1} K(M,n+1) for r < n, via the homology suspension (Freudenthal range).

The next page dualizes to F_p cohomology and stable operations, i.e. the Steenrod algebra (Steenrod–Epstein). Purpose: motivate the divided-power de Rham complex / Koszul–décalage formalism by the classical Dold–Puppe computation of H_*(K(G,n)).
errors: 'X un espace de Moore ZM(G,n)' conflates the Moore space M(G,n) with the simplicial abelian group Z M(G,n). The latter is ~ K(G,n), as stated correctly later on the page.
Dold–Thom gives reduced homology, H̃_i X. Basepoint conventions in Sym^∞X and in the identification Z[Sym^∞X] ≅ Sym(ZX) (quotient by basepoint) are glossed over.
The stable range is stated as r < n. This is the standard Freudenthal-type range up to off-by-one conventions; acceptable for lecture notes.
